findings.text: blocking: the docstring says the integer arrays are "compared against a plain host graph search over the same carrier and the same field the build was handed", but _assert_matches_carrier at lines 94-121 performs no graph search and never reads the field; it asserts that the receipt's own node_valid count exceeds its own edge_valid count by one and that its arc endpoints are valid rows. The test name test_sparse_build_matches_base_receipt likewise names a comparison against a base receipt the body no longer makes, so the file still does not measure what it claims, which is the defect this node was dispatched to repair.

blocking: the vertex_flux parameter of _assert_matches_carrier is supplied at line 194 and never used in the body, so the docstring's claim that the receipt's arcs bear the carrier's superlevel events is checked nowhere; a build returning the right node and arc counts over the wrong arcs, or the right arcs at the wrong carrier vertices, satisfies every assertion at lines 114-121.

blocking: the node's done_when asks for a reference that is the dense or brute-force build of the same field on the same host, compared array by array, and benchmarks/contour_tree_brute_force.py:216 already owns exactly that capability - compare(mesh, corrupt=False) is a plain host graph search over the carrier's own vertices and edges using only the mesh and the field values, covered by tests/test_contour_tree_brute_force.py; the landed check neither calls it nor extends it, replacing the named reference with a weaker structural assertion.

follow-on: _perturb_arc_order introduces a second env-var mutation selector, CONTOUR_TREE_ARC_PERTURB=rewire, where the repository's existing declared-mutation idiom is CONTOUR_TREE_CORRUPT=drop-wall-joins at tests/test_contour_tree_brute_force.py:54-57; two selectors for one idea invite a red log that does not say which mutation produced it.

blocking: the added jax.jit wrapper is redundant, because build_contour_tree already carries @partial(jax.jit, static_argnames=("neighbour_capacity", "node_capacity", "edge_capacity")) at nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py:494 in the reviewed head and in the node's own base 4ff706d76, so the bare call the test made before the change was already compiled; the negative control at logs/negative-control-jit-branch-on-traced.log would redden identically against the base revision.

blocking: this paragraph states that the capacity test "called build_contour_tree directly, so it no longer exercised compilation though its name and docstring claim it; a jit-incompatibility in the build would have left it green"; at the node's base 4ff706d76 the build is already jit-decorated at nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py:494, so a jit-incompatibility would have reddened that test before the change and the cited regression did not exist in the form the paragraph records.

follow-on: negative_control_note reports the arc-drop mutation as failing "3 of 9" while the log it cites, logs/head-fleet-sparse-perturb.log, ends "4 failed, 5 passed in 197.67s" with EXIT=1 and names all four test_sparse_build_matches_base_receipt parametrisations, so the manifest understates the red arm it points a reader at.
